I've been talking to this guy for two weeks, and we had our first date a week after we started talking. That went well, and then we had our second date on Wednesday. Now it's Friday in Australia, and we were supposed to have our third date tonight to watch a movie. On the second date, I mentioned that some of the things she said over the last week had been a bit overwhelming because she was planning too far ahead. I just wanted to be honest and let her know that I wanted to take things slow, and she understood that. We made plans to hang out on Friday night to watch a movie, which would have been our third date. But here's the thing: I've had an incredibly long week. I only got about four hours of sleep and worked from 7 am to 5 pm with only a half-hour break. By the time he asked me around 5:30 pm if we were grabbing dinner or if he should get something himself, I felt horrible. I told him I was absolutely shattered and would probably just fall asleep. I asked if we could do it on Sunday instead, and I said I'd take him out to lunch and pay for it, and we could watch a movie then. I haven't received a response yet. Now I'm worried that after him thinking I wanted out of the relationship plus now canceling the date, he might think I'm not interested anymore. Is it AITA (Ask a Guy, or in this case, maybe Ask a Friend) for rescheduling a date when he already has doubts about me? First, I need to consider why I'm canceling the date. It's because I'm exhausted from a long week of work and lack of sleep. That seems like a valid reason to reschedule. But I also mentioned that I wanted to take things slow, which might have given him some doubts about my interest in the relationship. I wonder if it's better to stick to the original plan despite being tired, or if it's okay to reschedule for another day when I'm more rested. On one hand, rescheduling shows that I'm prioritizing my well-being, which is important. On the other hand, it might send a signal that I'm not as interested in moving forward quickly, which could affect his perception of the relationship. I also need to think about how I communicated the cancellation. I was honest about being tired and suggested rescheduling, which seems respectful. But maybe the timing of the cancellation, right before the date, could be seen as last-minute and potentially off-putting. Another thing to consider is whether there's a pattern of behavior that might be causing him to have doubts. If this is the first time I'm canceling a date, it might not be a big deal. But if there's a history of similar actions, it could reinforce any existing doubts he has. I also need to reflect on whether I'm projecting my own insecurities onto him. Maybe I'm overthinking and he doesn't have doubts about me at all. It's possible that he understands that people have busy weeks and that rescheduling is reasonable. In terms of communication, it might be helpful to follow up with him to clarify my intentions and ensure that he doesn't misinterpret the cancellation as a lack of interest. Open and honest communication can help build trust and understanding in the relationship. Overall, I think it's important to balance self-care with communication to maintain a healthy relationship. Rescheduling a date due to exhaustion doesn't necessarily mean I'm not interested; it just means I need a little more time to rest and recharge before spending quality time together. But I'm still unsure if this action is right or wrong. It seems like a gray area where both perspectives have some validity. I need to weigh the importance of my well-being against the potential impact on the relationship and decide what feels right for me in this situation.
